newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Treasury posts 0.54 pct/GDP H1 op deficit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Treasury posts 0.54 pct/GDP H1 op deficit.

text.p: Brazil's Treasury said it posted an operational budget deficit of 2.249 billion reais in the first half of the year, equivalent to 0.54 percent of gross domestic product.
The Treasury said in a statement that the January to June figure compared with a 0.41 percent of GDP operational budget shortfall in the same period a year ago.
The operational budget includes debt servicing costs.
Treasury budget figures reflect only spending by the National Treasury unlike those figures released by the Central Bank, which include the consolidated public sector result.

The Treasury said the primary result, which does not include interest payments, showed a 0.84 percent of GDP surplus in the six-month period to June, compared with a surplus of 0.71 percent in the same year-ago period.

In June 1997, the Treasury posted an operational deficit of 1.061 billion reais, slightly down from an operational budget deficit in June last year of 1.203 billion reais. In May of 1997, the operational deficit was 558 million reais.
In primary terms, the Treasury posted a 56 million real surplus in June compared with a 637 million primary surplus in May 1997 and a 540 million deficit in June 1996.
Total receipts in the January to June 1997 period were 52.442 billion reais, versus 49.689 billion reais in the January-June 1996 period.
Total expenditure in the first half of this year was 48.306 billion reais, of which 20.617 billion reais went toward payroll.
In the first six months of last year, total expenditure was 46.834 billion reais, of which 22.337 billion reais was payroll.

Real interest payments on Treasury debt between January and June this year totalled 6.385 billion reais with 1.117 billion reais of that coming in June. In the same period last year, the Treasury spent 4.512 billion reais on real interest payments.
